issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named Meal with constructor Meal(String, String[]), but the template repository does not provide an implementation for Meal.java (it's empty) and instead contains an Order.java class with the same shape. This name/type mismatch (Meal vs Order) is structural and will confuse students about which class to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a Meal.java implementation in the template matching the problem statement (Meal(String, String[]) with getters). Either remove or clearly justify the presence of Order.java (e.g., rename Order.java to Meal.java), so the class names in the template align with the specification and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution refer to the domain entity as 'Meal', but the template repository provides an 'Order' class (and leaves Meal.java empty). This naming mismatch (Meal vs Order) makes it unclear which class students should use or implement and increases cognitive load when mapping the problem requirements to the provided starter code and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier: either provide a Meal class in the template (move/rename the existing Order class to Meal and populate src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java), or update the problem statement and solution to consistently use 'Order' instead of 'Meal'. Preferably, rename the template's Order class to Meal so the starter code matches the problem description and the solution reference.
